name: Career Survival
instruction: Use one Agent and all four supplied Skills. At a fresh entry, read Career Controller and all three specialist Skills with skill_tool before the first game action. After continuation or context loss, reload Career Controller and any needed Skill body that is no longer available. For gameplay, use only the five native Career Emulator tools: show_employee_handbook, new_game, observe, take_action and check_latest_logs. Select the exact registered tool from the live tool list; treat tool identifiers as opaque and never type or rebuild them from memory. If a call is explicitly rejected before dispatch because its tool identifier is unregistered, discard that identifier, refresh/select the matching live registered entry, and reconcile the same game session and current state. If the rejection confirms no action committed and the choice remains legal, retry using the registered entry. Repeat this recovery when each failure is confirmed pre-dispatch; there is no fixed retry-count limit. Never repeat the rejected identifier. For timeouts, post-dispatch errors or ambiguous results, reconcile first and do not retry until execution status is clear. Do not use alternate clients, shell commands, subprocesses or direct database access for gameplay. Career Controller is the sole coordinator and executor; specialist Skills advise and do not execute actions or rewrite Skills. Use only the confirmed game session_id returned by new_game; never create another game on continuation or while identity/execution is uncertain. Observe before each action and after every successful action. Reconcile failures before deciding again; never replay a cached choice. Optimize the final competition score. Use the published qualitative importance to guide priorities: Level is marked Higher, Wealth High, physical/mental wellbeing and professional skill Medium, and risk control and coworker relationships Some weight. Treat these as distinct outcomes, not interchangeable raw points. Do not invent exact cloud weights, formulas or promotion thresholds, or assume local report weights carry over. Compare actions using verified direct effects and supported implications for survival, promotion, future pay and remaining time; keep unknown benefits unknown. Prevent early failure and clearly evidenced major irreversible losses. Ordinary risks are trade-offs, not automatic vetoes.
